Purdue aggressively promoted OxyContin to physicians, downplaying its addictive potential and encouraging high-dose, long-term prescriptions. Internal documents revealed deceptive tactics, including funding biased research and paying doctors kickbacks. This contributed to a surge in prescriptions—from about 670,000 in 1997 to over 15 million by 2002—driving widespread addiction and the broader opioid epidemic.

The family reaped billions in dividends from OxyContin sales, which peaked at over $3 billion annually. Estimates suggest they extracted at least $10-13 billion from Purdue between 2008 and 2019 alone, much of it transferred offshore amid growing scrutiny.

A few cases involve founders or executives:
- John Kapoor and Insys Therapeutics: Kapoor, the founder (not a multi-generational family operation), led aggressive promotion of Subsys (a fentanyl spray), including bribing doctors for prescriptions. Insys paid $225 million in settlements, and Kapoor was convicted of racketeering in 2019, serving prison time. Profits from these tactics contributed to over-prescription of fentanyl products.

Broader industry accountability includes multi-billion-dollar settlements from firms like Johnson & Johnson ($5 billion national settlement) for supplying raw opioid ingredients and deceptive marketing.

If Jaguar were to produce such a vehicle, here’s a detailed narrative of how it could be positioned and characterized: Overview and Design Philosophy The Jaguar V-Pace represents a daring expansion of Jaguar’s lineup — a sophisticated, performance-oriented MPV that bridges the gap between a luxury SUV and a grand touring estate. Built on the JLR D7a aluminum-intensive platform, the same architecture underpinning the F-Pace and XF, the V-Pace merges lightness, rigidity, and dynamic balance with family versatility. The design language draws from Jaguar’s latest styling evolution — muscular yet elegantly proportioned, with a long hood, a sweeping roofline, and a gracefully tapered rear. The V-Pace appears more like a "grand tourer for families" than a typical people carrier. Exterior Design From the front, the V-Pace wears Jaguar’s signature grille and feline LED headlamps, giving it a confident, assertive stance. Aerodynamic sculpting flows from the hood along taut shoulder lines, emphasizing both strength and elegance. The side profile shows a sleek roofline that subtly arches toward the rear, maintaining a sense of movement even at rest — a hallmark of Jaguar’s “Grace, Space, Pace” ethos. The rear design is distinctly sporty, featuring slender taillights inspired by the F-Type, a subtle roof spoiler, and a quad-exhaust layout that underscores its performance credentials. Chrome accents and flush door handles reinforce its premium British character. The British Racing Green metallic finish shown in the images enhances its aristocratic presence, harmonizing beautifully with the countryside setting — a nod to Jaguar’s heritage of blending performance with refinement. Interior and Cabin Design Inside, the V-Pace offers a sumptuous yet purposeful cabin, balancing contemporary technology with timeless craftsmanship. The interior shown features Windsor leather upholstery in a two-tone mix of Forest Green and Oyster, with precision-stitched detailing, dark walnut veneers, and satin metal trims. The dashboard architecture mirrors that of the XF and F-Pace, with the Pivi Pro infotainment system at the center — a crisp touchscreen interface complemented by physical rotary controls for climate functions. The rotary gear selector rises elegantly from the center console, and the digital instrument cluster provides driver-focused clarity. Seating is arranged in a 2+3+2 configuration, offering true MPV practicality with fold-flat rear rows. Despite its family focus, the driving environment remains distinctly Jaguar: intimate, sporty, and sophisticated. A panoramic glass roof floods the cabin with natural light, while ambient LED lighting sets a refined tone for evening drives. Practical touches like multiple USB-C ports, a cooled glovebox, and configurable storage modules make it an ideal grand tourer for modern families. Powertrains and Performance The V-Pace’s dynamic capability is central to its identity. Two members of the Ingenium engine family power the range: The 2.0-liter AJ200 inline-4 turbo produces 296 hp and 400 Nm of torque, delivering effortless acceleration and refined cruising performance ideal for urban and long-distance travel. For those seeking greater performance, the 3.0-liter AJ300 twin-charged inline-6 — enhanced by a 48V mild-hybrid system — produces 400 hp and 550 Nm of torque, enabling sports sedan levels of responsiveness while maintaining superior fuel economy and lower emissions. Both powertrains are paired with a 9-speed ZF automatic gearbox, renowned for its smoothness and precision. Power is sent to the rear wheels by default, emphasizing traditional Jaguar driving dynamics, while an optional all-wheel-drive system with adaptive torque distribution ensures optimum traction and stability in all conditions. Adaptive Dynamics suspension continuously monitors road conditions and driver inputs, providing a balance between comfort and agility rarely found in MPVs. Technology and Safety The Jaguar V-Pace would serve as a showcase of the brand’s latest innovations. Features such as AI-driven driver assistance, Predictive Energy Optimization, and a full suite of ADAS systems — including adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, and 360° camera — enhance safety and ease of driving. Jaguar’s InControl suite offers seamless smartphone integration, over-the-air updates, and remote vehicle control via mobile app. Optional rear entertainment screens, Wi-Fi hotspot capability, and a premium 1200W Meridian surround sound system with 18 speakers turn the cabin into a rolling lounge of refinement and connectivity. Driving Experience and Positioning Unlike conventional family movers, the V-Pace would be tuned for dynamic confidence. The low center of gravity, lightweight aluminum structure, and precise steering deliver a level of composure and engagement rare in this segment. It’s an MPV that can whisk a family across the countryside in quiet luxury yet still handle a winding road with the precision expected of a Jaguar. The V-Pace would occupy a unique niche — a luxury performance MPV offering sitting alongside mainstream rivals like the Mercedes-Benz Citan Tourer, yet sportier and more emotionally engaging than the F-Pace or Range Rover. It would appeal to families and professionals seeking space, craftsmanship, and performance without compromise. Narrative Summary In essence, the Jaguar V-Pace reimagines what a luxury MPV can be: elegant, exhilarating, and deeply emotional. It’s a vehicle for those who value both grand touring spirit and everyday practicality, an embodiment of Jaguar’s timeless creed — Grace, Space, Pace — evolved for the modern era of refined versatility.

text: All of my favorite lower body openers wrapped up into one post! These 5 tend to get the best responses from clients as well. Save this one for when ya need it! 1️⃣ Banded Hip Distraction: If your hips always feel jammed up & tight - you should try this one! The band allows for the hip joint to gap/distract/open up more, so it’s great if your hips are feeling jammed and stiff. I usually start with ~1 minute at a time, but you can really work up to 5 minutes + if you want! 2️⃣ Banded Quad Opener: The bench allows you to fully relax the down leg which will help you get the most out of the stretch. Squeeze the glute to really feel the front of the hip open up! One of my favorites! 3️⃣ Banded Frog Distraction: A great hip opener for before or after your lower body day, or just if the hips fell tight & stiff. Place the band around your waist line, get on all 4s with your toes pointing out, & sink your hips back. Feel free to make it more active by driving the hips forward & then sinking back more, or keep it completely passive & relax! 4️⃣ Banded Elevated Pigeon: One of my favorites! The incline bench allows the knee to fully rest which allows for a better stretch - something we often don’t consider when doing this stretch in other positions. 5️⃣ Banded Hip IR (Supine): A great primer to “grease the groove” before squatting. While you internally rotate your hip, the band will help distract the hip joint to create some space which allows the hip to internally rotate better. Make it active by bringing the hip to neutral then back to IR, hold IR for :30-:60 seconds, etc. Play around with it! Most of these can be done passively or actively. I suggest doing both - but most importantly if you can, follow it up with movements that are typically stiff to see if helps! BMS talk for TYs On Tuesday 21st October 2025, we welcomed representatives from Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) Cruiserath Biologics to speak to TYs - Lorraine Kelly and Donal Monaghan. Bristol Myers Squibb is a global biopharmaceutical company whose mission is to discover, develop and deliver innovative medicines that help patients prevail over serious diseases. The visitors spoke to TYs about the career opportunities across multiple functions, including Biologics Manufacturing, External Manufacturing and Commercial. TYs learned that BMS first began operations in Ireland in 1964 with an Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient Plant (API) in Swords, County Dublin. The current BMS operations in Ireland include a newly constructed state-of-the-art biologics drug-substance manufacturing facility in Cruiserath, Dublin 15 and External Manufacturing divisions in Blanchardstown, Dublin 15 and Shannon, Co. Clare. BMS Ireland employs approximately 650 people. The TYs also learned about the pathways each of the 2 employees went on since college, which was really interesting. The company collaborates with second level institutions, particularly those with a core focus on STEM subjects. Their TY programme is an exciting week-long programme of activity for TY students with an interest in learning more about a career in science, engineering and the pharmaceutical sector in Ireland. A number of TYs have applied for this programme so hopefully a student will get a place. BMS also offer an Apprenticeship Programme designed to offer hands on experience and a robust foundation for individuals eager to embark on a career in the pharmaceutical industry. This is done through structured education, formal training and learning in the workplace. It takes 2 years to complete the Level 6 qualification, with an optional third year for those pursuing a Level 7 qualification. Thanks to Lorraine and Donal for visiting ACS. We really appreciate your time.

It’s Precision Medicine Awareness Month, and GCCA would like to thank the sponsors of the Know Your Biomarker Program. Precision medicine and biomarker testing can match patients with targeted therapies that will work best for their specific cancer. Know Your Biomarker is an awareness, education, and advocacy campaign promoting global access to colorectal cancer biomarker testing. Doctors on Ground at the One Young World Summit 2025 Through the AstraZeneca Young Health Programme (YHP) Impact Fellowship, Doctors on Ground (DnG) was represented at the One Young World Summit 2025 in Munich by our Founder, Arissa Jemaima. This year, Arissa joined the Summit as an AstraZeneca Delegate, part of the organisation’s largest delegation to date—100 leaders, including 12 YHP Impact Fellows and 87 AstraZeneca colleagues from around the world. The Fellowship and Summit provided a critical platform to showcase Malaysia’s community-driven health work and to highlight #JagaJiran, DnG’s flagship community-based Community Health Navigator (CHN) ecosystem. JagaJiran aligns strongly with AstraZeneca’s priorities in youth health and NCD prevention, as well as One Young World’s commitment to scalable, people-centred innovation. Across the week, DnG engaged in discussions on health equity, systems leadership, gender, community resilience, and decentralised care — connecting Malaysia’s on-ground realities with global health agendas. What’s next for DnG: We will be focusing on strengthening and scaling JagaJiran, expanding CHN training pathways, formalising global partnerships, and deepening our research on community health, gender, and NCDs. The goal remains the same: to build a sustainable, community-led ecosystem that ensures care is accessible, shared, and sustained where people live.

This is not an actual vaccine in the sense that it is administered as a cancer preventative.  

Pembroria’s active ingredient, pembrolizumab, is bioequivalent to Keytruda (Merck/MSD’s branded version, approved in Vietnam since 2017). As such, its efficacy mirrors extensive global data from Keytruda’s clinical trials and real-world use—no new, Russia-specific efficacy trials for Pembroria were required for approval, per Vietnam’s Drug Administration. 

Still, pembrolizumab is highly effective for many advanced cancers but is not a cure-all—response rates vary by cancer type, stage, patient genetics (e.g., PD-L1 expression), and combination with other therapies (e.g., chemotherapy). It is most beneficial in second-line or adjuvant settings.

The Google Pixel 10 Pro XL and Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra are two of 2025’s most advanced Android smartphones, both offering flagship performance and cutting-edge camera technology. While they compete in the same premium space, each takes a different approach to photography, display, and user experience, making them suited to different types of users. The Pixel 10 Pro XL features a 6.8-inch OLED display with a 120 Hz refresh rate and high peak brightness, delivering sharp visuals and smooth scrolling. Its rear camera system includes a 50 MP main sensor, a 48 MP ultra-wide lens, and a 48 MP telephoto lens with 5× optical zoom. This combination, paired with Google’s renowned computational photography, produces consistent, balanced images with excellent dynamic range. One of its standout features is the 42 MP front camera, significantly higher in resolution than most competitors, making it ideal for selfies, video calls, and social media content creation. The device is powered by the Tensor G5 processor and up to 16 GB of RAM, ensuring smooth multitasking and efficient handling of AI-driven features. The 5,200 mAh battery supports 45 W wired charging and Qi2 wireless charging, providing reliable all-day endurance. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra Overview The Galaxy S26 Ultra offers a 6.9-inch Dynamic AMOLED QHD+ display with 120 Hz refresh rate and exceptional brightness and contrast, ideal for media consumption and detailed photo/video review. Its rear quad-camera system is highly versatile: a 200 MP main lens, 50 MP ultra-wide, and two telephoto lenses (3× and 5× optical zoom). This setup allows for wide-angle, zoomed, and detailed shots, providing unmatched flexibility for photography enthusiasts. While the front camera is 12 MP, slightly lower than the Pixel, it is sufficient for standard selfies and video calls. Under the hood, the S26 Ultra runs on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, offering top-tier performance for gaming, content creation, and heavy multitasking. Its 5,000 mAh battery is slightly smaller than the Pixel’s but optimized for balanced usage.

text: On May 24, 2025, the World Health Assembly adopted a historic resolution on rare diseases — the first global recognition of the need to include this community in public health policies, information systems, universal health coverage, and international collaboration. With support from AstraZeneca, the Americas Health Foundation (AHF) and Enfermedades Raras en el Caribe y América Latina - ERCAL convened a hybrid regional forum that brought together international experts, policymakers, and patient advocates from across Latin America and the Caribbean to discuss how to turn this global resolution into concrete national actions. This milestone marks an unprecedented opportunity for Latin America to advance equity in diagnosis, treatment, and access for people living with rare diseases. By fostering dialogue between governments, technical experts, and civil society, AHF continues to bridge science, policy, and impact across the region. AHF is committed to expanding this work — and we invite partners who share our vision of health equity to join us in driving forward inclusive, sustainable rare disease policies in the Americas. text: Do I really need to tell you we're winning today? Come now - it's the Boks' green hydra gargling French tears in Turin, facing down an Azzurri no longer under the radar. We've got the scalps, the depth dialed deep, and the skulls geared to jam into the cogs. No sidestepping blood if glory's the game. No, you don't need me to spell it; you know it bone-deep like a Bok tackle - what your skeleton feels like inside your flesh - that innate certainty perfumed with the thrill of the unfolding. To some, it'll always look like arrogance. But is it not the simple math of momentum meeting the momentary, the inevitable echo from events? If I'm going on tangent, it's because Italy believes this is their shot - the outsiders' dream. And they're right. It's a dream. Everyone will want to put their hand up today, stain the jersey with their blood. Repeat lineups are recipes for rust, sayeth Rassie. Complacency embarrassed us earlier this year against Australia at Ellis Park, but truth be told, the cracks were hairline against Italy - despite nulling them with 14 men last. We're making amends well when required this year, and with grievances, the minds of the fresh charges look well framed. Add to this a bench that chews souls, and Italy's dream sours quick. We won't be taking them easy, but take them we will, one way or another. The wordless wink this week: Do we really need adversity to thrive? Against Italy no less... It's a mythological trap that could one day undo us. Personnel's not the main puzzle - the mind's contingencies win this war. Do we need the brink to bite? Boss from boot to buzzer, no flirt with the fall? Warp-spasm our weird wingman, or bad Bok habit? Must we dip to better soar? Pondering that's pure luxury. That's how far we've come. Prediction: Boks 49-17. Forza? Nah - voetsek, victory! #Springboks #Bokke #ItalyVsBoks #RassieRiddle #Rugby #TurinTest #WarpSpasm #WhatsNotToLove #VoetsekVictory

text: To get all my FB friends filled in on what my last month was like… here we go !!! On October 17th late Friday my right leg including my foot swelled dramatically. I wasn’t’ sure what it was & hoped it would pass, and it didn’t so Monday I called 911 and was rushed to ER at Lutheran General Hospital where I was diagnosed with a major +DVT (Deep Venous Thrombosis) which in lay terms is a blood clot. I was immediately put on blood thinners (LMW-Heparin ie. Lovenox). Ultra sound & CT scans revealed a clot starting below my knee in my calf, leading up my thigh all the way into my inferior vena cava, along with a few pulmonary embolisms (thankfully non-life threatening due to their placement). Surgery was scheduled first for Wednesday the 22nd but finally happened Thursday the 23rd. I basically had a human RotoRouter performed where one orthoscopic went in behind my right knee & a second came in from up high in the top of my neck. Both would meet in the middle and the surgeon said the clot they pulled out was over 3 ft long. Also the neck probe went over to my left leg to remove some residual clotting I had there as well.. (I had been plagued with some edema in my feet off and on, for quite a while, thinking it was water retention not knowing it was actually clots). I was released from the hospital on Wednesday afternoon the 29th and have been on home rehab since. I get around with a walker due to the pain & swelling still present in my right leg which is slowly going away. I am thankful for all the prayers & support from everyone & my close friends (you know who you are) have been fantastic with my home support. I will be on blood thinners (DOACs,direst oral.. Eliquis) for at least several months. I have another CT scan scheduled for Nov. 22nd to see if all clotting has cleared. I’m here, I survived, by the grace of God & again I am grateful for all the DR’s, Nurses NA’s and all around me. I’m getting home PT and a nurse visiting a few times a week so I’m on the mend. And yes, I’m back to work (at home which is normal) as best I can handle. So there you have it !!

text: 🌱✨ “Do good even when no one is watching — your character is louder than applause.” ✨🌱 💛 In this world where everyone wants to be seen, liked, praised, and celebrated 👀📸… there is something rare and powerful about being good quietly. Something beautiful about choosing kindness even when there is no audience 👥, no cameras 📷, no applause 👏. It’s in those silent moments — those unseen seconds — where your TRUE character shows 🌟💛. 🌙✨ When you choose patience over anger 😤➡️😌, love over ego 💔➡️❤️, and truth over convenience 🚫➡️✔️… even when no one knows about it… that’s when you grow. That’s when your soul becomes stronger 💪, softer 💖, kinder 🌿, wiser 🧠, and more grounded 🌍. 📖💫 Your story is not written by who praises you… but by how you treat people behind closed doors, how you behave when your name isn’t being called, and how you act when there’s nothing to gain 🌈. 🕊️✨ Being good in private is a form of integrity that can’t be faked. It doesn’t need an audience. It doesn’t need validation. It doesn’t need attention. It simply grows from the heart 💗 — from a place of sincerity, g Somewhere along the way, I stopped needing everyone to understand me. I stopped over-explaining my silence, my choices, my healing, and my boundaries. Growth taught me that peace doesn't come from being heard by the world — it comes from finally listening to yourself. I’ve faced storms I never saw coming and walked through seasons I never thought I’d survive. I’ve smiled with a heavy heart, showed up with shaking hands, and kept going when my soul was tired. That’s strength — the kind that no one claps for, but that changes everything. I’ve lost people, moments, and parts of myself I thought I’d never get back. But in that loss, I found clarity. I found self-resp. I found God in the silence, and power in becoming someone new. So no, I’m not the same. I don’t react the same. I don’t chase the same. I’m learning to protect my space, to pour into what pours back, and to love without losing m Healing isn’t pretty. It’s not always soft. Sometimes it looks like pulling away, crying in silence, or outgrowing people you love. But I’ve made peace with that. Because every time I chose myself, even when it was hard, I became more whole. I don’t have all the answers. I still have scars. But I’m proud of the person I’m becoming — someone who values peace over attention, depth over surface, and alignment over approval. This chapter is no longer about proving my worth. It’s about living in it. So if you’re in a quiet season, one where everything feels uncertain — don’t give up. Sometimes, the most powerful transformations happen when no one is watching. I no longer chase what doesn’t choose me. I no longer explain what peace feels like to people committed to chaos. My silence is no longer discomfort — it’s my healing. It’s my clarity. It’s my protection. I’ve outgrown the version of me that begged for love, settled for less, and called it loyalty. I now understand that not everyone is meant to go with me — and that letting go doesn’t mean I stopped caring. It means I started caring for *me*. I’m learning to be okay with being misunderstood. With being distant. With being selective. Because not everyone deserves access to the version of me I worked so hard to rebuild. I walk differently now — not because I think I’m better, but because I know I’m worth more. And I’ve earned the right to protect my energy, set my standards, and speak only when it matters. This isn’t just a new season — it’s a new standard. And from here on out, anything that costs me my peace is too expensive. I’ve realized that becoming isn’t loud. It doesn’t always look like success, trophies, or applause. Sometimes it’s just choosing not to react. Choosing rest instead of burnout. Choosing solitude over fake support. And that’s growth too. The kind no one sees — but *you* feel. So now, I move with intention. Not to prove anything, not to chase anything — but to protect the peace I fought so hard to find. No more begging to be seen. No more shrinking to be liked. No more explaining to be understood. I’m not becoming who the world expects. I’m becoming who I *need*. And that, for me, is enough. This is the season where I water myself. Where I trust the slow days, the silent shifts, and the sacred space in between. Because real growth? It doesn’t always shout. Sometimes… it just *blooms quietly*. I no longer rush healing. I no longer rush life. Everything meant for me will arrive in peace, not pressure. So I’m learning to breathe. To be fully present. To find beauty in the now — even if it’s messy, quiet, or unfamiliar. Some days, I still feel lost. Some days, I overthink. But even on those days, I’m proud — Because I no longer abandon myself just to feel accepted. I show up for me now. Gently. With grace. With patience. With truth. And if you’re on this journey too — You’re not late. You’re not behind. You’re not broken. You’re becoming. And that’s the most courageous thing of all. So keep softening without losing your strength. Keep glowing, even if no one notices yet. Keep walking — even when your voice shakes. Because your becoming is valid. And your peace is sacred. I’ve come to accept that not everything will make sense right away. Some chapters only reveal their purpose after the pain. Some people were lessons, not lifetimes. And some endings were really just beginnings in disguise. But through it all — I kept rising. Not because it was easy, but because something in me refused to give up. I owe that version of me… the one who held on silently… everything. So from now on, I celebrate the quiet wins. The boundaries kept. The healing I chose. The peace I protected. The love I gave myself when no one else knew I needed it. Because true strength isn’t loud. It’s soft. It’s sacred. It’s steady. I’m not chasing the spotlight anymore. I’m chasing alignment. I’m chasing purpose. I’m chasing peace. And in doing that — I’ve finally found *me*.#fblifestyle I mean always Always put yourself first ✨💛… because your heart, your peace, and your dreams deserve priority 💗🌙. Too many times you’ve carried people, situations, and problems that were never yours to hold 😔🧳. Now it’s time to carry yourself — with love, with care, with strength, and with pride 💪🏽❤️👑. Putting yourself first is not selfish 🚫😤… it’s self-respect 🙏💎. It’s understanding that you cannot pour from an empty cup 🍶❌. You deserve to wake up with peace 😌🌤️, go through your day with confidence 💃🔥, and sleep knowing you chose what’s best for your soul 🛌💫. When you protect your energy ⚡🛡️, you protect your future 🌈🌱. Choose the things that help you grow 🌿✨. Choose the people who uplift you 🤝💖. Choose the boundaries that keep your heart safe ❤️‍🛡️. Walk away from anything that confuses your spirit 😮‍💨💔, drains your joy 🥀😩, or makes you doubt your worth 😔🚫. You are not here to be broken; you are here to shine 🌞💫. Remember, healing takes time 🕊️⏳, but every small step you take for yourself is a victory 🏆💛. Celebrate your progress 🎉🌟, even the quiet moments no one sees 👀✨. Keep believing in the person you’re becoming — stronger 💪🔥, wiser 🧠💡, softer where it matters 💗🌸, and sharper where it’s needed ⚔️✨. Your journey is yours alone 🚶‍♀️🌌. People may not understand your choices, and that’s okay ✅🙂. What matters is that you understand your purpose, your value, and your direction 🎯🌟. Don’t fear letting go of what no longer fits — the moment you release what’s heavy, life becomes lighter 🌬️🤍. So choose yourself unapologetically ❤️🙌. Speak kindly to yourself 🗣️💗, trust your growth 🌱✨, and honor the love you carry inside 🧡🔥. Keep shining, keep rising, keep becoming the version of you that you’ve always dreamed of 🌞🌻💫. text: Truth vs Fiction I take a multivitamin daily so I’m getting what my body needs nutritionally. Absolutely false. Nearly all big name multivitamins are made by Big Pharma. Centrum is made by Pfizer. One A Day is made by Bayer. Nature Made is co-owned and produced by Bristol-Myers-Squib. These “vitamins” are produced for profit, not your health. The ingredient label says it all. Calcium carbonate is typically the first ingredient. That’s limestone folks and is not easy for your body to breakdown. This is not the same calcium found in milk. Magnesium oxide is next. This form of magnesium has the absolute lowest absorption rate at about 4% of any magnesium and provides little to no benefit. Maltodextrin is almost always there as well. Maltodextrin is a highly refined sweetener made from trash corn. It is highly toxic to the liver due to its ultra processed nature. No one, and I mean no one should consume maltodextrin. BHT is also likely found in a lot of vitamin supplements and is very controversial currently as a likely hormone disruptor. The companies producing this garbage have a long history of legal issues and lawsuits but due to the lack of FDA regulation, they continue to be allowed to market these “vitamins”. If you chose to supplement, do your homework. Look for the USP seal on the label. This means the product was tested by the United States Pharmacopeia and meets quality standards for absorption and bioavailabilty. That means your body actually can absorb and use the labeled ingredients. Look at the ingredients. Look at third party testing and testing for heavy metals. It’s always better to get vitamins and minerals from food but if you choose to supplement, do your homework and don’t put garbage in your body that is labeled as “natural” or “healthy”.

Healthcare is broken Healthcare in costs in America is a tragedy 🤬🤬🤬🤬🤬 A U.S. government study found that in 2022, U.S. drug prices were on average ~229 % of Canadian prices (i.e., Canadian prices were about 44 % of what Americans paid) for the same drugs. Another review noted that for brand-name drugs, U.S. prices can be ~3 to 4 times higher than in Canada (or higher, depending on the specific drug). For example: Eliquis (a blood thinner) costs in the U.S. ~$1,668 for 180 tablets, while in Canada the lowest listed price was ~$370. Jardiance (for diabetes) cost ~$1,845 in the U.S. for 90 tablets versus ~$290 in Canada. An analysis found that Rinvoq (for Crohn’s/ulcerative colitis) is ~$11,915 in the U.S. vs ~$1,749.95 in Canada — roughly 7× the Canadian price. ⚠️ Examples of drugs with large U.S.–Canada price gaps Eliquis: ~4.5× higher in the U.S. vs Canada. Jardiance: ~6×+ higher in the U.S. vs Canada. Rinvoq: ~7× higher. In a broader list: Latuda (an antipsychotic) 90 tablets cost ~$4,628 in U.S., ~$520 in Canada (~89 % cheaper in Canada). Synthroid (for hypothyroidism) cost ~$114 in U.S. vs ~$44 in Canada (≈ 160 % higher in U.S.) in one older study. 🧠 Why does this happen? Canada uses government regulation and negotiation to constrain prices for patented drugs; the U.S. historically has fewer nationwide restrictions on drug manufacturer pricing. Brand-name drugs (patented) show the largest price gaps; generics often have smaller or even reversed differences. A study found that in 2017 the U.S. spent US $2,497 per person on health-care administrative costs, compared with US $551 per person in Canada. That’s more than 4× the Canadian per-capita amount. The source pointed out that if the U.S. reduced administrative costs to Canadian levels, it could potentially save over US $600 billion annually. Interpretation: A large chunk of U.S. spending is not directly care for patients, but overhead, billing, management, insurer profits, etc. 🔍 Example 2: Overall Spending and Payments to Providers The U.S. spends roughly twice as much per person as “peer” countries (including Canada) when it comes to health care. Much of the difference comes from higher payments to hospitals, physicians, and higher prices for services — not necessarily more services. For example: A source reports that the U.S. was spending ~16.8% of GDP on healthcare vs Canada’s ~10.8% (in one comparison) with the U.S. per-person cost at ~US $10,948 vs Canada ~US $5,370. 🔍 Example 3: Drug Pricing & Provider Mark-Ups While this example is more indirect, a recent report by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) found that U.S. pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) marked up prices of specialty generic drugs by thousands of percent between 2017-2022, leading to multi-billion-dollar gains. Higher negotiated prices, mark-ups, and less regulation in the U.S. contribute to higher profits in the supply chain. 🔍 Why This Shows Higher Profits (and Costs) If administrative/overhead costs are dramatically higher in the U.S., that means a larger portion of healthcare dollars is going to management, insurers, bureaucratic functions, profit margins — rather than directly to clinical care. Higher per-person payments to hospitals and physicians suggest that U.S. providers can charge (and are paid) more for the same or similar services. Higher drug mark-ups and profit-oriented structures in the U.S. supply chain mean more of the spending ends up as profit (or margin) rather than being passed on in lower consumer/patient cost. When you combine these factors, you end up with a system where expenditures are high, yet outcomes (on many measures) are not better (and in some cases worse) compared to Canada. For instance, Canada often achieves similar or better outcomes at lower cost. ✅ Summary Yes — there is strong evidence that the U.S. healthcare system enables higher profits and overheads (for insurers, administrators, providers) compared to Canada, which contributes to the much higher cost burden on U.S. patients and payers.

Michael Burry bets against the AI rally: Scion Asset Management puts 66% of its portfolio into Palantir $PLTR put options.

The "Big Short" investor also bought Nvidia $NVDA puts at 13.5%, shorting the two hottest AI infrastructure plays. 

Meanwhile, he went long on Pfizer $PFE calls at 11.1% and Halliburton $HAL calls at 4.5%.

Burry sold UnitedHealth $UNH, Regeneron $REGN, Lululemon $LULU, and Meta $META calls. His portfolio turnover was 95%—essentially starting from scratch. 

This comes as Palantir reported beats on Q3 results: $1.2B revenue, up 63%. The stock is up 270% this year. Burry clearly thinks it's gone too far.

AI is writing more than ever, but here's why human expertise is still the secret sauce:

After years leading medical writing at Pfizer & Sanofi, I saw the immense complexity. When I founded DIP, my vision wasn't to replace human writers, but to empower them. Our AI crafts regulatory documents, protocols, and translations with incredible speed & accuracy. 🚀

But the magic happens when human experts guide the AI. They provide the scientific narrative, ensure critical thinking, and apply nuanced judgment that only a human can. It's a powerful collaboration: AI handles the heavy lifting, humans ensure scientific excellence and compliance. Think of it as a super-powered co-pilot, not an autopilot. 🧠✍️

This synergy is how we achieve zero-defect documents and faster submissions. It's not AI vs. human; it's AI + human for better science. What are your thoughts? 👇

text: Grrrrr president trump!! Nonprofit hospitals and health clinics are alarmed about a change that's coming to federal drug purchasing discounts next year. They'll have to pay up front and then get rebates — rather than direct price cuts — in a pilot with eight pharmaceutical companies. Why it matters: The new system, greenlit by the Trump administration, is a win for drugmakers, and it could be a big hassle for providers. Under the test, which starts in January, providers will pay full price for drugs they currently get at a steep discount. They'll get reimbursed the difference after the drugmaker determines they qualify for the lower price under the 340B program, which allows nonprofit safety net providers to access lower-cost outpatient drugs. What they're saying: "Many hospitals are concerned about cash flow around this," Maureen Testoni, CEO of the provider trade group 340B Health, said on a recent call with reporters. Providers will have to hire new staff to submit data to get the rebates, or at least shift employee responsibilities around, she said. She noted that the change comes as providers prepare for cuts to Medicaid reimbursement and other likely changes that could reduce their Medicare payments. Where it stands: The Health Resources and Services Administration last week approved 340B rebate programs for nine popular drugs, including Bristol Myers Squibb's blood thinner Eliquis and Janssen's Stelara and Xarelto. The pilot will run for at least one year to test whether rebates work for 340B discounts, HHS said in July when it first announced the idea. PhRMA sees the rebate pilot as a step toward more transparency and accountability in the 340B program, senior director of public affairs Molly Jenkins said in a statement. The administration should go further and allow rebates across all 340B-covered outpatient drugs, Jenkins added. Several pharmaceutical companies have tried to implement their own rebate systems in recent years, arguing they guard against providers getting duplicate discounts or diverting 340B drugs to ineligible patients. Courts have so far blocked them from doing so without HHS approval. Yes, but: The nonprofit health system Advocate Health says the savings from direct discounts allow it to invest $6 billion annually into free clinics, charity care and community-based programs. "A shift to a rebate model, as opposed to the current discount model, would undercut our ability to continue this level of care," the health system's leaders wrote in a comment letter to HHS earlier this year. The rebate model "is a clear case of the fox guarding the hen house," Jennifer DeCubellis, CEO of America's Essential Hospitals, said in a statement, adding that "drug manufacturers are the only winners" of the program. The other side: HHS maintains that the pilot is a limited, data-driven effort to improve 340B, press secretary Emily Hilliard told Axios via email. HHS is undertaking the project to "better understand the merits and shortcomings of the rebate model from the perspective of affected stakeholders," she wrote.

With tears of gratitude, I want to formally announce the arrival of Ramon to the United States. I am literally indebted with my life to this lady who had faith in us to co-sponsor him. You are our hero, my lifeline, our hope Joy Liebfreund Seagraves. Muchisimas gracias de mi corazon! I have been getting treatment at The OSU James Cancer Center for follicular lymphoma (FL) cancer since 2020. I have failed three types of chemo and my FL has transformed into aggressive diffuse large b cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Cancer has progressed to my lungs. It was not possible for me to start with Breyanzi CAR-T treatment unless I could guarantee to my hematologist that I had someone with me 24/7 for a minimum of one month (given any unforeseen circumstances). This procedure called "apheresis" begins on December 5th with extracting my t-cells (via a pic line) for submission to Bristol Meyers Squibb (BMS) for genetic modification in their laboratory. This is to make a man-made protein on the surface of the cell called chimeric antigen receptor (CAR). These receptors are designed to bind the surface of the cancer cells, which lets the modified T cells attack them like Pacman. The CAR-T cells fight the cancer and help protect against the return of cancer. The CAR-T cells are multiplied, frozen and sent back to the hospital. During this process I will continue to have cycles of chemo to get rid of the remaining cancerous T cells. After the T-Cells are received from BMS, I will receive them as an outpatient. This process is not without serious risks of Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS), Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), neurological toxicity, risks of infection and/or other side effects, hence, the reason for having someone by my side 24/7. We must live within 30 minutes of the clinic in the event of a crisis. The James will provide our hotel stay in Columbus. The risks are very frightening but it is our hope that CAR-T will allow me more time with Ramon as there is no cure for blood cancer. I appreciate all the love, support and prayers that you all have provided. Please don't stop now as this new chapter will be a delicate process. Pray with us that there will be no or few complications and limited stress for Ramon as my caretaker. We appreciate your support in my previous post "We Got This" to help with expenses and needs while in Columbus without cooking facilities and in our journey in the road ahead. I would be remiss not to acknowledge the help of Ellen, immigration case manager, in Senator Bernie Moreno's office. Her patience and perseverance in communicating with me and the US Embassy in Santo Domingo enabled Ramon to receive an expedited family visa (though we had been in this process for 6 disappointing years). Also, with the help of letters and the pathology report from my doctor, Ramon is with me. He is 100% legal in the US with a green card and social security card to work when that time comes. For now, our focus is on my health. That will be a job in itself! LOL! To this end, if it weren't for Joy's sponsorship of Ramon, my hope of an extended life would not be possible. Ohh, we give our gratitude to all who have donated winter clothes to Ramon. He arrived with a small luggage full of summer clothes. He is now prepared for winter, thanks to many. Our first snowfall he was like a little kid running from window to window to see the snow and calling all his family on Messenger live chat to show them the white stuff. It brought me so much happiness! So much to be thankful for! Give Thanks To Life and Great Friends! We Got This! We love you, Joy!

With patients typically receiving six treatments annually, that’s around $76,100 per patient. With the standard 20% Medicare Part B coinsurance, that means roughly $15,000 annually in out-of-pocket costs for patients enrolled in Original Medicare, aka traditional Medicare, without supplemental coverage. What Medicare enrollees should do now Review your supplemental coverage. If you have traditional Medicare without Medigap coverage, the 20% coinsurance on Part B drugs like Keytruda could mean roughly $15,000 annually. text: Prof Uzma Firdaus Appointed Chairperson of AMU’s Department of Paediatrics ALIGARH, November 24: Prof Uzma Firdaus of the Department of Paediatrics, Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College, Aligarh Muslim University, has been appointed Chairperson of the department for a three-year term beginning November 24. An accomplished clinician and academician, Prof Firdaus brings 18 years of teaching experience to the role. Her areas of specialisation include neonatology and developmental paediatrics. Prof Firdaus serves as the Nodal Officer for the District Early Intervention Centre and the Centre of Excellence established under the Rashtriya Bal SwasthyaKaryakram (RBSK), National Health Mission. She has also completed a major multicentric research project on severe pneumonia in children under the IndiaCLEN and MCH STAR initiative. Her academic profile includes 40 research publications in national and international journals, 25 presented papers, three published books, and extensive involvement in postgraduate thesis supervision. She has received several prestigious recognitions, including the Prof R.S. Dayal Gold Medal in Neonatology, the Dr Hadi Hasan Memorial Medal, and the Pfizer Award, along with multiple university medals and distinctions. Prof Firdaus is trained in Paediatric Advanced Life Support (PALS) and Neonatal Advanced Life Support (NALS) and is a certified trainer for the NavjaatShishu Suraksha Karyakram (NSSK). Public Relations Office Aligarh Muslim University

This trial combines DATROWAY with an immunotherapy drug called Durvalumab (a drug similar to Keytruda). Science is constantly advancing and there are currently limited options for TNBC. The really good news here is that we have another much-needed treatment option for Triple Negative Breast Cancer. text: Merck is testing a new pill called enlicitide that can lower “bad” cholesterol a lot—about half or more. It could be the first easy-to-take PCSK9 pill, instead of shots, to help keep hearts healthy.

Yes, vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT/TTS) was causally linked to adenovirus-vector COVID-19 vaccines like AstraZeneca and J&J, with incidence rates around 1-10 cases per million doses, prompting updated warnings in 2021. Regulatory bodies like the EMA and FDA confirmed benefits far outweighed these rare risks, as vaccines prevented millions of deaths from COVID-19. Withdrawals stemmed from commercial shifts to updated mRNA vaccines, not safety revocations.

text: A BMS most commonly refers to a Building Management System (also called Building Automation System or BAS). Here's a clear overview: ### What is a BMS? A Building Management System is an integrated computer-based control system installed in buildings that monitors and controls the building’s mechanical and electrical equipment such as: - HVAC (heating, ventilation, and air conditioning) - Lighting - Power systems - Fire systems - Security systems (access control, CCTV) - Lifts/elevators - Water supply and plumbing - Energy metering ### Main Functions of a BMS 1. Centralized Control – Operators can monitor and control all systems from a single interface (usually a software dashboard). 2. Energy Management – Optimizes energy use (e.g., turns off lights/HVAC in unoccupied areas, adjusts temperature setpoints). 3. Alarm Management – Detects faults (e.g., pump failure, high room temperature) and alerts operators. 4. Data Logging & Trending – Records historical data for analysis and reporting. 5. Scheduling – Automates routines (e.g., office lights on at 7 AM, off at 7 PM). 6. Remote Access – Many modern BMS allow control via web or mobile apps. ### Common BMS Protocols - BACnet (most widely used open protocol) - Modbus - LonWorks - KNX - DALI (for lighting) - OPC ### Major BMS Manufacturers/Brands - Siemens (Desigo) - Honeywell (EBI, ComfortPoint) - Schneider Electric (EcoStruxure, Andover Continuum, TAC) - Johnson Controls (Metasys) - Tridium (Niagara Framework – integrator platform) - Distech Controls - Trend Controls - Delta Controls - Automated Logic (WebCTRL) ### Other Meanings of BMS (context-dependent) - Battery Management System – Used in electric vehicles and battery storage (monitors cell voltage, temperature, state of charge, etc.). - Business Management System – General term for integrated business software. - Bristol-Myers Squibb – Pharmaceutical company (stock ticker BMS). - Burner Management System – Safety system for industrial boilers/furnaces. If you’re asking about a specific type (e.g., building BMS, EV battery BMS) or need details about integration, programming, or a particular brand, let me know and I can go deeper!

text:
AstraZeneca hits record high, cements lead as UK’s biggest stock

Shares in AstraZeneca rose past their September 2024 peak on Tuesday, hitting a fresh record high and cementing the company’s position as the largest UK-listed stock by market value.

Tuesday’s surge added to the rally after forecast-beating quarterly earnings last week and a U.S. drug-pricing deal in October that helped remove some policy uncertainty. The United States accounts for more than 40% of AstraZeneca’s total sales.

By 08:32 GMT, AstraZeneca was up 2.5% after surging to as high as 134.6 pounds, giving it a market value of close to 210 billion pounds ($282 billion).  The blue-chip FTSE index, meanwhile, rose 1.1% to new record highs of its own, after UK labour market data boosted expectations for a Bank of England rate cut next month.

($1 = 0.7451 pounds)

text: WASHINGTON (AP) - President Donald Trump unveiled a deal Thursday with drugmakers Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk to expand coverage and reduce prices for their popular obesity treatments Zepbound and Wegovy. The drugs are part of a new generation of obesity medications known as GLP-1 receptor agonists that have soared in popularity in recent years. But access to the drugs has been a consistent problem for patients because of their cost - around $500 a month for higher doses - and insurance coverage has been spotty. Coverage of the drugs for obesity will expand to Medicare patients starting next year, according to the administration, which said some lower prices also will be phased in for patients without coverage. Starting doses of new, pill versions of the treatments also will cost $149 a month if they are approved. Thursdays announcement is the latest attempt by the Trump administration to rein in soaring drug prices in its efforts to address cost-of-living concerns among voters. Drugmakers Pfizer and AstraZeneca recently agreed to lower the cost of prescription drugs for Medicaid after an executive order in May set a deadline for drugmakers to electively lower prices or face new limits on what the government will pay. As with the other deals, its not clear how much the price drop will be felt by consumers. Drug prices can vary based on the competition for treatments and insurance coverage. Obesity drugs have become increasingly popular, but are costly The obesity drugs work by targeting hormones in the gut and brain that affect appetite and feelings of fullness. In clinical trials, they helped people shed between 15%% and 22%% of their body weight -- up to 50 pounds or more in many cases. Patients taking these drugs usually start on smaller doses and then work up to larger amounts, depending on their needs. Because of obesity being considered a chronic disease, they need to take the treatment indefinitely or risk regaining weight, experts say. The fast-growing treatments have proven especially lucrative for drugmakers Eli Lilly and Co. and Novo Nordisk. Lilly said recently that sa #wsbtv #crimewatchatlanta les of Zepbound have tripled so far this year to more than $9 billion. But for many Americans, their cost has made them out of reach. Medicare, the federally funded coverage program mainly for people ages 65 and over, hasnt covered the treatments for obesity. President Donald Trumps predecessor, Joe Biden, proposed a rule last November that would have changed that. But the Trump administration nixed it last spring. Few state and federally funded Medicaid programs, for people with low incomes, offer coverage. And employers and insurers that provide commercial coverage are wary of paying for these drugs in part because of the large number of patients that might use them. The $500 monthly price for higher doses of the treatments also makes them unaffordable for those without insurance, doctors say. Medicare now covers the cost of the drugs for conditions such as type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease, but not for weight loss alone. Trump showing he is in touch with cost-of-living concerns The effort to lower costs barriers to popular GLP-1 drugs comes as the White House is looking to demonstrate that Trump is in touch with Americans frustrations with rising costs for food, housing, health care and other necessities. Republican gubernatorial candidates in New Jersey and Virginia faced a drubbing in Tuesdays election in which dour voter outlook about the economy appeared to an animating factor in the races. Roughly half of Virginia voters said the economy was the top issue, and about 6 in 10 of these voters picked Democrat Abigail Spanberger for governor, powering her to a decisive win, according to an AP voter poll. In New Jersey, Democrat Mikie Sherrill won about two-thirds of voters who called the economy the top issue facing the state, the poll found. She defeated a Trump-endorsed Republican candidate Jack Ciattarelli. More than half of New York City voters said the cost of living was the top issue facing the city. The Democratic mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani won about two-thirds of this group. The White House sought to diminish the effort by the previous Democratic administration as a gift to the pharmaceutical industry because the proposal did not include adequate price concessions from the drug makers. Trump, instead, consummated a belt and suspenders deal that ensures that Americans arent unfairly financing the pharmaceutical industrys innovation, claimed a senior administration official, who briefed reporters ahead of Thursdays Oval Office announcement by Trump. Another senior administration official said coverage of the drugs will expand to Medicare patients starting next year. Those who qualify will pay $50 copays for the medicine. Lower prices also will be phased in for people without coverage through the administrations TrumpRx program, which will allow people to buy drugs directly from manufacturers. starting in January. The officials said lower prices also will be provided for state and federally funded Medicaid programs. And starting doses of new, pill versions of the obesity treatments will cost $149 a month if they are approved. The officials briefed reporters on the condition of anonymity under ground rules set by the White House. Doctors applaud the price drop Dr. Leslie Golden says she has roughly 600 patients taking one of these treatments, and 75%% or more struggle to afford them. Even with coverage, some face $150 copayments for refills. Every visit its, How long can we continue to do this. Whats the plan if I cant continue., said Golden, an obesity medicine specialist in Watertown, Wisconsin. Some of them are working additional jobs or delaying retirement so they can continue to pay for it. Both Lilly and Novo have already cut prices on their drugs. Lilly said earlier this year it would reduce the cost of initial doses of Zepbound to $349. The potential to cover the medication for the 30 million people on Medicare who have obesity would be welcome, said Dr. Fatima Cody Stanford, an obesity expert at Massachusetts General Hospital. But until details are released, she remains skeptical. I would have to see it to believe it, she said. I need to see something that is more definitive for Medicare beneficiaries. I need to see something that is tangible and sustainable. Dr. Angela Fitch, who also treats patients with obesity, said she hoped a deal between the White House and drugmakers could be the first step in making the treatments more affordable. We need a hero in obesity care today, said Fitch, founder and chief medical officer of knownwell, a weight-loss and medical care company. The community has faced relentless barriers to accessing GLP-1 medications, which has ultimately come down to the price, despite the data we have supporting their effectiveness. ✨️💖New Week, New Strength, New Spark💖✨️ As soon as we pulled into Smilow for treatment today, my phone rang — it was Yale’s CAR-T Cell Therapy team calling to schedule Mom’s consultation. Mom was already anxious about how treatment would go, and that call piled worry right onto her racing mind. She looked confused, scared, unsure why this was happening. ✨️✨️🙏🙏💖💖✨️✨️ Walking into treatment was stressful. Once she got back in the chair, her weight was solid — a big win — but her blood pressure was sky-high. She takes it three times a day, and she hasn’t been on her BP meds since she got sick. It rattled her. It rattled me. But later at home? Her BP was completely normal again.✨️✨️🙏🙏💖💖✨ No updates today about starting Cytoxan since Revlimid has been halted. That adds to her anxiety. So we’re still waiting on that direction. Between the CAR-T call and all the uncertainty, the whole appointment hit heavy. ✨️✨️🙏🙏💖💖✨️✨️ On the ride home, she started tearing up. Everything caught up to her. I held her hand and brought her back to right now — reminded her she’s safe, she’s guided, and she is absolutely not alone. Then something incredible happened. She started reading about CAR-T… about how many high-risk patients have gone into deep remission… and I watched her Spark flicker back to life.✨✨✨ By the time we got home, she felt encouraged, hopeful, and ready to talk about the positive impact this treatment could bring. I told her to get on her stepper to clear her mind — she always feels mentally stronger after she moves her body. And, even after everything today threw at her, this woman crushed a full hour on that stepper. That’s warrior-level determination. ✨️✨️💖💖🙏🙏✨️✨️ I’m so proud of her. She’s fighting physically, mentally, emotionally, spiritually — harder than ever. And today, despite the fear and the chaos, my beautiful fighter reignited her Spark. ✨️✨️✨️✨️✨️✨️✨️✨️✨️✨️ Sparktastic job today, Mom. I love you. Always, always. XOXO. 💖✨️💖✨️💖✨️💖✨️💖✨️

Today is Stomach Cancer Awareness Day! The Power of Periwinkle™ campaign has been illuminating landmarks and sites around the world since 2017! ✨ This campaign is about raising awareness for our cause. It is also about bringing our community - patients, survivors, caregivers and healthcare providers - together no matter where we live in the world. 🌎 As we see sites illuminate to support us we are empowered, we honour those on the journey and we remember those who are no longer with us. We know that together we are stronger and our voice is being heard! Our new interactive map shows the illuminated sites, so we welcome you to take a look, click on a city and enjoy the beauty and hope of The Power of Periwinkle™!! Thank you to our sponsors, our illuminating and community partners over the years! A very special thank you to all the cities and sites that have illuminated and thank you to all who have volunteered! Check out our NEW INTERACTIVE MAP now and explore all of the sites around the globe that have lit up in Periwinkle to support Stomach Cancer Awareness Day and the Power of Periwinkle! ⬇️ https://www.mygutfeeling.ca/stomach-cancer-awareness-day. Today, as we commemorate World Diabetes Day, we are reminded that diabetes remains one of the most urgent health challenges in our country. Its growing prevalence affects families, communities, and our entire healthcare system. That is why our mission is clear: Prevention must be our priority. This Agham Kapihan, together with Diabetes Philippines and AstraZeneca Philippines , marks an important milestone as we officially launch the STOP DIABETES: ACT NOW Program. This initiative highlights the need for early action, because diabetes and its complications can be prevented when we intervene early, educate communities, and empower patients to take control of their health. We also recognize the vital support of Philippine Health Insurance Corporation , whose YAKAP Program strengthens early diagnosis by providing essential tests for high-risk individuals. Early detection saves lives, reduces complications, and prevents many Filipinos from progressing to kidney disease and other serious outcomes. Most importantly, today is about partnership. We stand here together with patient groups, the Philippine Diabetes Support community and the Dialysis PH Support Group Inc. We remind that the fight against diabetes and chronic kidney disease is not only a medical battle, but a personal one. 🤝 When government agencies, healthcare providers, patient groups, and private organizations unite, we create a stronger, more hopeful path forward. Together, we can stop diabetes. Together, we can protect Filipino families from CKD. Together, we act now. Thank you, and may this Kapihan inspire stronger collaboration and real change for all Filipinos at risk and living with diabetes. #WorldDiabetesDay2025 #TaraNaStopDiabetes 🖐 #ACTNow P. S Nice meeting you all What's Up Today , Mommie Kleyrr #nofussmom, and FPJ Jr . It was a great discussion with you about Diabetes prevention and Kidney health. We hope we can work together to help spread accurate information on the importance of prevention and proper health management. Looking forward to future collaborations! - Reynaldo Segarra Abacan Jr. President of Dialysis PH ( Kabato Rey )

Today l had the pleasure of hosting Chairman of Merck Foundation Board of Trustees Professor Dr Frank Stangenberg-Haverkamp and Senator Dr Rasha Kelej, CEO of Merck Foundation and President of the “More Than a Mother” campaign.

We shared the milestones we achieved in healthcare, media, and girls’ education among other sectors over the past 7 years. Together, we are building a stronger, healthier, and more educated Zimbabwe for the future.

I am glad that our partnership through my Angel of Hope Foundation has resulted in Zimbabwe benefitting 166 scholarships empowering doctors in critical and underserved specialties such as diabetes, cardiology, oncology and fertility.

What is more pleasing is that our all weather friend Merck Foundation has doubled our yearly scholarships from 20 to 40 due to our strong dedication over the years.

As a champion for women empowerment l am also glad that through our partnership “Educating Linda” programme also continues to support 40 underprivileged high-performing girls yearly.

text: Know Your Lung Health💚 Lung health matters more than ever. Our partners at SGH are seeing more cases of breathlessness, asthma-like symptoms, and the rising effects of vaping; so we put together a half-day programme to equip our seniors with the knowledge they need. Held in conjunction with World COPD Day, the session focused on spotting early signs of chronic respiratory conditions and understanding why early detection can be life-changing. All in all, it was about breathing better, living better, and taking charge of our own health. Our next session will be on SLEEP! Why some experts believe that sleep is more important than food?☺️ 🌿Special thanks to our partners; Team SingHealth, Team SGH, Sanofi, SGO, Unisoy, GSK & AstraZeneca for showing up so strong for our residents! #lunghealth #agewelllivewell

"

text: Greetings everyone, Having never been a Facebook user I decided based on current life changes that it is time to start. I have been, to my mind, happily married for the last 5.5 years to Mickey Regenold. A nurse I worked with at Park Center prior to my wife of 21 years dying of Cancer in 2018. To my great surprise Mickey told me one month ago she was divorcing me. No discussion and no explanation. To this day I do not know why she is divorcing me. But it is clear that our time together has come to an end. I will walk away with gratitude for the 7 years we have shared together and with love in my heart. The following changes are in motion. Divorce will be final on Jan 15, 2026. I am buying a house in Kendallville, IN which is only about 8 miles from where I work. It should close on 12/15/25 and I anticipate moving in over Christmas s. I work at a CMHC as a psychiatrist and I work M - Thursday. I am also a national speaker for Bristol Myers Squibb on their new Schizophrenic drug, Cobenfy. On the personal side I have concluded that the main reason the marriage failed was because of a lack of good communication. Wherever something came up that involved any emotions, Mickey would shut down and refuse to talk about it. Over 5 years this amounted to more and more broken communications that could never have a complete cycle to finish them. I believe this broke the marriage. There are more issues that involve personal history which I am not at liberty to discuss. I will be looking to explore future relationships. Important issues for me are: #1 good communication, #2 I enjoy touch and have felt a severe absence of this in my marriage, $3 I would enjoy being able to discuss politics - for this reason I will not date anyone who voted for Trump. I understand that living in Indiana this limits me to a much smaller percentage of the populaton - but I accept that. Such is my update for now.

text: First Lady Lordina Mahama Inspires St. Mary’s School Girls, Donates Learning Materials The First Lady, Mrs. Lordina Dramani Mahama, has encouraged pupils of St. Mary’s Basic and JHS at Korle Gonno to remain confident and rise above stereotypes that limit girls. During her visit, she presented essential learning materials and engaged with beneficiaries of the Educating Linda Programme, a Merck–Lordina Foundation initiative supporting girls from disadvantaged backgrounds. Twenty outstanding students have so far received scholarships through this partnership. Her message was clear: “Do not be intimidated because you are girls. Be confident in your abilities.”

Hi, fam and friends. As some of you may have known, I was diagnosed with Stage 3 Cecal Mucinous Adenocarcinoma (Colorectal Cancer) last November 2022. I have tried herbal medicines for a while, but unfortunately, none of them have worked for me. My oncologist then advised me to undergo immunotherapy as he believes this is a better approach considering the type of cancer I have. It took my family some convincing, but finally, they agreed to let me pursue this treatment. I have high hopes that this would work for me, but I have to admit, I'm super worried as this therapy is expensive. We’re happy to be able to get a discount for Keytruda Patient Access Program (KEYPAP), the medicine for the treatment. However, even with this discount, the costs are still significant due to the number of sessions I need to complete (4-6 sessions every three weeks) and the frequency of PET CT scans required for reevaluation. We’re also applying for government assistance but we’re unsure if help would arrive on time. In light of this, I find myself humbly reaching out for your support. Any financial help you can offer would greatly help as I begin with the treatment. And if you could keep me in your thoughts and prayers, that would mean so much. I know so many of us are facing tough times and I sincerely wish our circumstances are better.. So truly, thank you so much for your kindness and taking the time to read this. When Josephine Dickson's kitchen accidents became a regular occurrence in 1920, her husband Earle created a solution that would change first aid forever. Earle was a cotton buyer for Johnson & Johnson in New Jersey. He noticed his wife was always cutting or burning her fingers while cooking. Back then, dressing a small wound by yourself was a clumsy process, involving separate gauze and tape. So, Earle came up with a simple idea. He took a long strip of his company's adhesive tape, laid a strip of gauze down the middle, and covered it with crinoline fabric to keep it sterile and prevent the adhesive from sticking to itself. Now, his wife Josephine could simply cut off a piece and apply a bandage herself whenever she had a minor accident in the kitchen. 🩹 He showed the invention to his bosses at Johnson & Johnson. They were impressed by the simple practicality of the idea and decided to produce it. The first commercial "Band-Aids" were sold in 1921. Sales were slow at first, though. The first year, they only sold about $3,000 worth of the new product, because most people were not yet familiar with the idea of a pre-made bandage. The company didn't give up. They decided to give them away to Boy Scout troops and butchers to demonstrate their usefulness. The strategy worked, and popularity soared. 🇺🇸 That small solution, born out of a husband's care for his wife, is now found in nearly every home, school, and workplace in the country. A true American success story. Sources: Lemelson-MIT Program, National Inventors Hall of Fame, Johnson & Johnson website

#NTH_CARES BRONCHOSCOPY MACHINE BOOSTS LUNG CANCER DIAGNOSTICS AT NDOLA TEACHING HOSPITAL ======================== Ndola Teaching Hospital has strengthened its respiratory diagnostic capacity following the official handover of a bronchoscopy machine and accompanying digital equipment valued at over K700,000. The donation was made through the Multinational Lung Cancer Control Program (MLCCP), implemented by Access to Health Zambia and Zambart, with support from the Bristol Myers Squibb Foundation. Speaking during the ceremony, Copperbelt Provincial Health Director, Dr. Charles Mwinuna, represented by Dr. Nasilele Simushi, described the donation as a major step toward improving early detection and management of lung cancer, tuberculosis, and other respiratory conditions on the Copperbelt. He said the bronchoscopy machine represents more than a technological upgrade, stressing that it symbolizes progress, innovation, and the power of collaboration in improving public health outcomes. “Bronchoscopy is a critical diagnostic tool that enables clinicians to detect lung abnormalities early. By enhancing diagnostic capacity here in the Copperbelt, we move a step closer to reducing the burden of respiratory diseases and improving patient outcomes,” he said. Dr. Mwinuna applauded Access to Health Zambia and Zambart for their leadership in research and health system strengthening, stating that their partnership with Ndola Teaching Hospital demonstrates how collaboration can deliver meaningful healthcare solutions. He urged the hospital’s management and clinical staff to ensure optimal use and proper maintenance of the machine to improve service delivery. “As we receive this bronchoscopy machine, let us renew our commitment to advancing health equity, investing in technology, and building a resilient healthcare system for the people of Zambia,” he added. Access to Health Zambia Chief Executive Officer, Mrs. Batuke Walusiku-Mwewa, said the donation aligns with national efforts to combat cancer and expand specialized healthcare services. She highlighted that the partnership with Zambart and the Ministry of Health under the MLCCP has strengthened cancer awareness, trained community health workers, and expanded lung cancer screening in Ndola and Kabwe. “As part of this ongoing work, we are proud to hand over a bronchoscopy machine, laptops, tablets, and a desktop computer to enhance diagnostics, data management, and research,” she said. Zambart Executive Director, Dr. Kwame Shanaube, commended the partnership, noting that improved diagnostic equipment is essential for reducing delays in lung cancer detection and improving treatment outcomes. She emphasized that bronchoscopy capacity at Ndola Teaching Hospital will help reduce misdiagnosis and delays in patient care. Meanwhile, Ndola Teaching Hospital Acting Head Clinical Care, Dr. Tela Bulaya, thanked Zambart, Access to Health Zambia, and the Bristol Myers Squibb Foundation for the donation, describing it as a milestone in advancing the hospital’s respiratory services. “For years, patients suspected of having lung cancer or other respiratory complications had to be referred to Lusaka at great financial and emotional cost,” she said. “Today, that burden has been lifted. This machine brings life-saving diagnostic services closer to the people.” Dr. Bulaya assured partners that the equipment will be properly maintained and fully utilized, supported through continuous staff training. She also acknowledged the efforts of the Internal Medicine, Respiratory, and Biomedical Engineering teams whose dedication made the milestone possible. The newly commissioned bronchoscopy machine is expected to significantly improve diagnostic accuracy, reduce referral delays, and strengthen Ndola Teaching Hospital’s role as a regional centre for specialized healthcare services. By :Ndola Teaching Hospital Public Relations Department

Glad to see you back first of all. I went to a wedding 10/31/23, came home showered and felt like I couldn’t breathe. To the ER I went and found out I had 2 blood clots in my right lung. Never ever had I thought. Been on Eliquis since🤦🏾‍♀️

Monday Morning Check-In 🩺☕ Today is treatment day for Mom, and after the tooth extraction and infection, we’re feeling extra grateful that she’s still able to receive her infusion. 🙏 We’re not exactly sure what to expect with stopping Revlimid and possibly adding Cytoxan, but we’re walking in with: an open mind faith in God and His will and trust in her team to guide us toward whatever is most effective for her treatment plan 💉✨ I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t anxious about the tumor board on Wednesday… but today, we’re staying right here in this moment. One hurdle at a time. One step, one lab, one infusion at a time. 💪 Sending hugs and healing prayers to everyone walking their own hard road today. You’re not alone. 🙏🙏🙏💖💖💖✨️✨️✨
